23. It is now well settled that the PWDV Act is a civil law remedy available in a criminal court.

The proceedings are predominantly civil in nature, because the reliefs provided under Sec. 18 to 23 (protection order, residence order, monetary relief, custody, compensation, etc.) are all civil remedies.
However, the provisions of the Act are enforced through the criminal courts and breach of a protection order is made a criminal offence u/s. 31 of the Act.
24. So as to make out a case under the PWDV Act and to get the relief under the said Act, the Kajal vs Deepak Jaiswal on 4 December, 2025

sentences.text: 25. So as to attract the provisions of PWDV Act and to seek relief under the Act, the first and foremost requirement is that the complainant must fall within the category of 'aggrieved person', as defines u/s. 2(a) of the Act.

As per u/s. 2(a), "aggrieved person" means any woman who is, or has been, in domestic relationship with the respondent and who alleges to have been subjected to any act of domestic violence by the respondent.
Thus, to be an aggrieved person, the complainant must be or must have been in domestic relationship with the respondent.

Domestic relationship has been defined u/s. 2(f) of the Act, as a relationship between two persons who live or have, at any point of time, lived together in a shared household, when they are related by consanguinity, marriage, or through a relationship in the nature of marriage, adoption or are family members living together as a joint family, whereas, respondent has been defined u/s. 2(q) of the Act, as any adult male person who is, or has been, in a domestic relationship with the aggrieved person.

The term "shared household" has been defined u/s. 2(s) of the Act, as a household, where the person aggrieved lives or at any stage has lived in a domestic relationship either singly or along with the respondent.

23. It is now well settled that the PWDV Act is a civil law remedy available in a criminal court.
The proceedings are predominantly civil in nature, because the reliefs provided under Sec. 18 to 23 (protection order, residence order, monetary relief, custody, compensation, etc.) are all civil remedies.
However, the provisions of the Act are enforced through the criminal courts and breach of a protection order is made a criminal offence u/s. 31 of the Act.
ii. The respondent falls within the definition of 'respondent' u/s. 2(q) of the Act.
iii. There is existence of 'domestic relationship' between the parties.
By domestic relationship, it means that the parties are living or having lived in a 'shared household'.
iv.
25. So as to attract the provisions of PWDV Act and to seek relief under the Act, the first and foremost requirement is that the complainant must fall within the category of 'aggrieved person', as defines u/s. 2(a) of the Act.
Thus, to be an aggrieved person, the complainant must be or must have been in domestic relationship with the respondent.
In the present case, so far as the existence of domestic violence between the appellant no. 1 and respondents is concerned, same is not in dispute, as the appellant no. 1 and respondent no.1 got married on 08.12.2008 according to Hindu rites and customs and the appellant no. 1 resided with the respondents in the shared household.
